Messages.Author: ALLAN D JAKUBOWICZ
Messages.Body:
My question pertains to the "Cultivated Blood Shortage" card. 
This master card drains one blood from all Ventrue during the untap phase.
The card states: "... Any vampire can burn this card by taking a D action, 
                      which would be at +1 stealth."

I think that you can only burn the card if you have a vampire or a card that
gives you the capability of taking D actions (since the card states '... by
taking ...' and doesn't say '.... as a ...' ).
My friend argues that any vampire can burn the card and the action will be
considered as a direct action.

Can somebody please e-mail me the correct interpretation of the card.
Thanks in advance.

                         Allan Jakubowicz
                         cs922020@ariel.cs.yorku.ca

Messages.Author: Lucyred
Messages.Body:
Wich reminds me, is "cultivated blood shortage" a shortage of cultivated
blood, or a blood shortage which you have cultivated?

Also, many political cards say that you can burn them with a vote.
(Archon, Rumors of Gehenah) But aren't Political cards already in your
ashheap? Wouldn't that make the text on those cards totally meaningless?

Lucyred

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Minions always have available the actions in the rulebook, and any actions
provided by cards in play.  Actions of the latter kind are provided by
the card in question, and you don't have to burn an action card to take
advantage of them.

Most political cards just go to the ash heap when used.  But if some
condition is given for the card being burned or stolen, then it remains
in play.  Since Archon gives a condition for being burned, it remains
in play on the vampire in question.  This is the same principle as for
master cards; it just so happens that a higher percentage of master
cards stay in play.

Messages.Author: Lucyred
Messages.Body:
I want you all to know that I refuse to play with the AoR ruling, not
because I think that WotC sucks, or anything like that, but because I
can't. I play Jyhad with several people who lack a modem, and I can't
explain to them why the AoR works that way. It neither says that on the
card, or in the rules, and the card isn't even better than those dominate
bleed cards.
   The fact is: A good bleed deck can do thre plus bleed per action, and
that alows them to do much more than 1 point cumulative, with a one turn
delay. And the AoR can be swept. I truly don't see the problem.
   And when I do try to explain it, people accuse me of cheating, and I
don't blame them, _I_ feel like I'm cheating. The ruling doesn't make any
sense, and is not supported by anything. 
   I won't play with it, because I can't.


Lucyred

Another advantage of multiple rats is that it benefits Nosferatu and
Gangrel.  Under current rules, Gangrel make great combat decks, but combat
decks are mediocre with multiple players (albeit fearsome 1-on-1). 
Nosferatu have stealth, but it can be hard to find actions for them worth
making stealthy (Computer hacking for 2 bleed vs. Malkavian
Govern/Conditioning for 6(!)).  AoR adds to either clan, making them
better, but, as Lucyred points out, not killer.  I think that the game is
most interesting if all clans can be good, mulitplayer or single player,
without being killer.
